label: copy-phase input j, gated by which token follows j (e/j/t/z/c/y/0)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (96% of mass) on steps whose input is j, i.e. right after the model has re-emitted a j and is about to output the token that followed j in the original. Does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, or on a first occurrence of any token. A small remainder (about 4% of mass) is on input e. Only about 10% of copy-phase j inputs fire, though. Which token is being output next strongly modulates both the firing rate and the magnitude. The strongest activations (up to 1.0 of max) are j->e transitions, and more strongly so when the input before j was i or h (patterns like "i j e"). Next outputs j, t, z, c, y and 0 give weaker firing, and most other next tokens rarely fire. It is also suppressed when the j is at original position 0 or 1 (recall_idx <= 2) and peaks at recall_idx 3-4. The predicate (dev F1 0.52, mass recall 0.82) misses j inputs followed by other tokens that do fire weakly, and over-predicts many j->c/t/z cases that stay silent, so the selectivity is only partly captured.
